title: 1.1 Python fluency beyond the basics
description: Roadmap 1.1 — 12 topics, in the document's own order.
learningOutcomes: Take every topic in this section to pass 3 of the roadmap's rule: intuition, then derived on paper, then implemented from scratch.

lessons.title: Data model: __dunder__ methods, descriptors, __slots__
learningObjectives: Explain why special methods are looked up on the type and not the instance, and predict what that breaks
Implement the equality, hashing and ordering contracts correctly, including the trap that makes a class unhashable
Write a data descriptor and explain where it sits in attribute lookup precedence
Decide when __slots__ is worth it, and name three things it takes away
lessons.description: How Python's object protocol actually works — special-method lookup on the type, the equality/hash contract, descriptors as the mechanism under properties and ORMs, and what __slots__ really buys you.

lessons.title: Iterators, generators, yield from, lazy evaluation
learningObjectives: Distinguish an iterable from an iterator and explain why the difference causes the exhaustion bug
Write generators that hold state across suspensions, and know what yield from forwards that a loop does not
Predict when laziness saves memory, when it defers an error, and when it holds a resource open too long
Compose itertools pipelines and name the two functions that quietly break the memory guarantee
lessons.description: The iterator protocol, generators as suspendable functions, yield from and delegation, and the real trade-offs of laziness — memory, single-pass exhaustion, deferred errors and resource lifetime.

lessons.title: Decorators, closures, functools (lru_cache, partial, wraps)
learningObjectives: Explain what a closure captures, why it captures a variable rather than a value, and how to fix the late-binding bug
Desugar any decorator by hand, including stacked and parameterised ones, and predict the order they run in
Use functools.wraps correctly and name what is still broken without it
Choose between lru_cache, cache and cached_property, and state the memory and correctness traps of each
lessons.description: Closures as cells over an enclosing frame, decorators as the plain function application they actually are, and the functools toolkit — wraps, lru_cache, partial, singledispatch, cached_property — with the failure mode each one brings.

lessons.title: Context managers and contextlib
learningObjectives: Desugar any with statement into its try/finally equivalent and predict exactly when __exit__ runs
Implement both the class-based and generator-based protocols, and say which one a given job wants
Explain what returning True from __exit__ does, and why almost every correct __exit__ returns None
Use ExitStack, suppress, nullcontext and asynccontextmanager where a plain with statement cannot reach
lessons.description: The with statement as a protocol you can implement, what __exit__ can and cannot do about an exception, and the contextlib toolkit — contextmanager, ExitStack, suppress, nullcontext — with the failure each one hides.
